proposals.what_changes: Tightens the serving scope by raising the required local_robust_z_peak threshold above 3.0 so that only series with stronger extreme-local-deviation evidence are treated by outlier_mad.
proposals.expected_change: Series with modest z-peaks (near the current 3.0 floor) remain untreated and keep the raw pipeline; the treated set shrinks to strongly-deviating series, which should reduce the number of series damaged by over-aggressive outlier modification.

proposals.what_changes: Replaces the frozen single-step outlier_mad program with a single hampel_filter operator, a different outlier-removal mechanism that is more robust to local context and less prone to over-trimming.
proposals.expected_change: On series that outlier_mad left unchanged (or could damage), hampel_filter may produce corrections where detectable outliers are removed while preserving non-outlier structure, potentially gaining on series the current program neither helps nor recovers.

proposals.what_changes: Moves from a single outlier_mad step that repeatedly damages series to a gentler two-step replacement: hampel_filter to detect and smooth genuine outlier spans, then winsorize to cap residual extremes. This preserves the aggregate-gain mechanism of the current program while lowering the per-series and fraction-based harm it currently causes.
proposals.expected_change: On the treated set, mean aggregate gain should remain positive and close to the parent support gain while worst_harmed_fraction and worst_single_series_harm drop below the absolute bounds of 0.2 and 0.3, respectively. Because hampel_filter is less aggressive than outlier_mad on highly contaminated or level-shifted series, the treated high-z-peak series that currently absorb most of the harm should see smaller corrections.

proposals.what_changes: Swaps the globally frozen outlier_mad for a median based iqr step followed by a hamper filter. The intent is to detect outlier points with a more inter-quartile based threshold that is less influenced by skewed short spans, then to smooth only those isolated spikes rather than canceling every deviation. The stricter detection should leave more of the series structure intact, reducing treatment-induced damage.
proposals.expected_change: This candidate should leave the treated high-z-peak series mostly unchanged in terms of aggregate gain (the deleted outlier contribution is largely preserved by the gentler correction) while lowering worst_harmed_fraction and worst_single_series_harm below the parent's current levels. The filter stage is necessary to keep a distinct operator mechanism, so that the aggregate gain does not collapse to identity but the harm amplitude is bounded.

evaluations.what_changes: Moves from a single outlier_mad step that repeatedly damages series to a gentler two-step replacement: hampel_filter to detect and smooth genuine outlier spans, then winsorize to cap residual extremes. This preserves the aggregate-gain mechanism of the current program while lowering the per-series and fraction-based harm it currently causes.
evaluations.expected_change: On the treated set, mean aggregate gain should remain positive and close to the parent support gain while worst_harmed_fraction and worst_single_series_harm drop below the absolute bounds of 0.2 and 0.3, respectively. Because hampel_filter is less aggressive than outlier_mad on highly contaminated or level-shifted series, the treated high-z-peak series that currently absorb most of the harm should see smaller corrections.

actual_cost.counting: every physical fit, including the ones spent inside a call that then raised; no allowance carried over

ledgers.course_fits_cover: the delayed gate and the evaluation face
ledgers.support_fits_note: Support probe fits, counted only where the evaluator reported them; probes that reported none are counted as unrecorded rather than as zero.  Courses run before this counter existed have no Support line at all and their Support cost stays a derivation, not a reading
ledgers.baseline_note: the reference model, shared by every arm on a unit because it is cached per (executor, origin).  COMPLETED executions and cache hits are counted; they are not folded into support_fits and not priced, because the injected evaluator reports no fit count and charging a shared model is an open protocol question
ledgers.baseline_evaluations_is_not_a_fit_total: it counts completed reference evaluations, one per (executor, origin).  What each one costs the Consumer is not reported by the injected evaluator, so this line must not be read as, or added to, a total of Consumer fits
ledgers.unmeasured_cost_note: an evaluation that raised inside the Consumer had already spent an unrecoverable amount: scoped_evaluate reports consumer_fits only on a normal return.  Those are counted here as unmeasured rather than added to any total as zero
ledgers.why_no_llm_prompt_cache: wiring CachedAgentBackend would change what the arms are charged for and how their proposals diverge; it is not enabled for HEC-1 and its absence is recorded rather than left as a zero that looks like a miss rate

code_state.why: historical behaviour may only be explained with the code that produced it; where HEAD differs the current file is not used
